speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history. To further evaluate your right flank pain and hematuria, please describe the specific character of the pain (e.g., sharp, colicky, burning) and tell me if the pain radiates to your groin. Additionally, have you noticed any passing of "gravel" or stones, or any recent changes in your urinary frequency?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Nephrolithiasis (Kidney Stone).

The combination of recurrent UTIs, visible hematuria, and right flank pain is highly suggestive of a kidney stone, possibly complicated by a ureteral obstruction or a struvite stone given your infection history. I am requesting a Non-Contrast CT of the Abdomen and Pelvis to confirm the presence and size of any calculi.
